prs.title: [cd] Tolerate 409 when uploading preview tarballs
prs.author: eps1lon
prs.body:
A rerun or new run on the same commit currently reuploads and overwrites the tarballs. Mostly to accomodate full runs on a commit to get all the binaries (regular runs only build for Linux).

Instead, we'll soon return a 409 from the server so that a tarball can be served as immutable.

This PR makes the client resilient against 409s.

If we ever build different variants for the same commit, we should update the route instead to reflect different build variants. This is would be the better choice anyway so that you know what build variant is behind a commit.

prs.title: [PPF] Instant validation for `ensureStatic = "shell" | "prefetch"`
prs.author: lubieowoce
prs.body:
Adjusts Instant Validation internals to validate the `ShellStatic` stage instead of `ShellRuntime` when `ensureStatic >= "shell"`. If that's the case, the client will do a static request (and extract the shell from it), so the app shell cannot access session data (unlike the PPF default, where we use a runtime shell).

Note that in some cases, this might seem more restrictive than needed. For `ensureStatic >= "shell"`, the client will do a static prefetch that goes up to the `Static` stage which resolves more things, like static `params`, `prefetch()` ( in the `PrefetchStatic` stage) and `navigation()` (in the `NavigationStatic` stage). However:
1. The client expects to be able to rewind the static prefetch into a shell and reuse it across the whole route, so we should be validating that the shell is actually useful.
2. For `ensureStatic = "shell"`, we might still do a *runtime* prefetch (with `<Link prefetch={true}>`), which will not have `navigation()`, and validating `ShellStatic` catches that.

### Implementation notes

- I've renamed `RequestStore.needsAppShell` to `RequestStore.needsRuntimeShell` (undoing a previous rename), because the `ShellStatic` stage can _also_ be an App Shell, just not a _runtime_ one. The flag controls whether or not we're delaying link data until the runtime stages, which we don't need to do if the shell is static.
- If we have `ensureStatic >= "shell"` set, we _won't_ set `RequestStore.needsRuntimeShell` anymore, which means that the main rend
…(truncated)

prs.title: Use graph-backed codegen for client proxies and WASM loaders
prs.author: sokra
prs.body:
### What?

Generate **both RSC client-reference proxies and WebAssembly loaders** under their graph-backed wrapper module identities, using one shared, higher-level content helper. Remove both generated-path exceptions from `BindingUsageInfo::used_exports` and the earlier proxy-specific export filter.

### Why?

The wrapper is the module in Turbopack's graph, but its chunk item previously delegated code generation to a separately processed virtual JS module. Export-usage lookup for that proxy/loader missed the graph and fell back to “all exports used.” In a `sideEffects: false` barrel this could register a pruned client export and request a missing `<locals>` module ID. The WebAssembly loader had the same graph-identity mismatch, hidden by a separate filename-based fallback.

Canary's #99102 now guards against the client-reference missing-ID symptom by checking pruned references. This PR fixes the upstream identity mismatch instead so `expand_exports()` sees real usage; #99102's independent safety checks remain in place.

### How?

`chunk_item_content_with_code_from(graph_module, code_source, ...)` takes the generated source's analyzed program, references, exports, source map and async behavior while using the wrapper for the *whole code-generation module context*. Both client-reference and WASM wrappers call it. This replaces the public low-level `with_module_context` setter; it does not change module IDs, WASM output assets, React Flight registration, or the existing single
…(truncated)

prs.title: turbo-tasks-gc: Defer most aggregation graph management until after GC has settled
prs.author: lukesandberg
prs.body:
Fix AggregationGraph updates during GC.

During GC we aremoving a lot of edges so this can trigger a lot of aggregation graph churn.  Because of the highly parallel nature of GC this can end up with multiple queues fighting over updates which can exceed various retry limits and lead to things like trying to turn nodes into `followers` that are actively being deleted.

Instead we just don't rebalance the aggregation graph during GC, instead we buffer every `rebalance` request and set the `optimize` budget to zero.  Then after GC settles we process all the rebalances at once, taking care to filter out any tasks that have been since deleted.

Because GC is only removing edges it can lead to inefficient graphs (too many interior nodes) but not violate graph invariants.

Alternatives considered:

The initial idea was to ensure GC had finished with all 'children' of the node before processing rebalance requests, but this was only a partial solution (and complex!), since it didn't handle the case of an aggregating node having multiple children become collectible in the initial scan, this could still trigger 'optimization contention' and turning dead nodes into followers.

Testing:

The test/benchmark are enhanced to produce non-trivial aggregation graphs which improves test coverage (though the issue of racing deletes was trivially found by CI also)

prs.title: Turbopack: chunk each layout segment once in production
prs.author: sokra
prs.body:
### What?

Stops Turbopack from re-chunking every App Router layout segment once per page in production builds. The manually constructed server-utilities chunk group is now only created in development.

### Why?

A production build should chunk each shared layout segment exactly once. Instead, a layout segment was chunked again for every endpoint below it. On a small app with four endpoints, the root layout was chunked 4 times and a nested `dashboard` layout 2 times. The emitted output was still shared, so this was wasted build work rather than bigger bundles, which is why output-based tests never caught it.

Production already builds a single module graph for the whole app, so the module graph is not what differs between endpoints. The difference comes from the server-utilities chunk group that seeds the layout-segment chain:

- It is a `SharedMerged` group whose parent is the current endpoint's entry chunk group.
- A merged group's parent is part of its identity, so every endpoint gets a different group (5 chunkings on the same app).
- Its result seeds the availability info passed to each layout segment after it. Availability info is part of the chunking task key, so each shared segment ended up with a different key per endpoint and was chunked again.

The code comment already said this manual shared chunk exists mainly to help development. That makes sense there: each endpoint has its own module graph in development, and without the group layout segments would share very l
…(truncated)

prs.author: gnoff

## Summary

Avoid decoding route parameters a second time while selecting prerender metadata. This fixes valid percent-containing URLs returning 500, including both build-generated closed routes and runtime-generated open routes.

For example, a request for `/open/docs/space%20here/with%2Fslash/fallback%25` is already normalized for manifest lookup before reaching `PrerenderManifestMatcher`. Test the existing, lazily constructed route regular expression directly instead. Matcher precedence, source-page filtering, and the current server parameter encoding behavior stay unchanged. This does not introduce a new manifest or adapter contract.

The open fallback is requested twice to cover generation and reuse. The existing fixture uses `dynamicParams = false` and remains excluded from the Cache Components matrix, which does not support that configuration.

This is an independent prerequisite for #97393: the failure reproduces without the parameter-matching API and should be fixed for existing apps too.

## Verification

- Before the fix, the new closed and open catch-all requests returned 500 with a parameter-decoding error. After the fix, both return 200 and retain the existing encoded server parameter values.
- The focused matcher unit suite passes all

prs.title: turbo-tasks-gc: Invalidating a deleted task should be a no-op
prs.author: lukesandberg
prs.body:
Make invalidating deleted tasks a no-op.

Invalidators now represent a 'weak' reference to a task, and invalidations don't assert task existence.  We know that the task exists when the invalidator is created but by the time an invalidation occurs it might not exist anymore.   So treat the dependency as weak.

Take care to not create 'blank' tasks when querying for them, this can confuse assertions that occur later.

## Why is this safe?

Currently it is safe because we never reuse task ids, so invalidating a deleted task is perfectly reasonable, much like invalidating a non-active task, there is nothing to do

In the future if we start reusing task ids, then this becomes an ABA problem.  An invalidator can point at a new task.  This is also not too bad, a spurious invalidation is self healing.  Also most invalidators are not actually persisted which limits the risk.

So we can either decide to build a mechanism to tear down these stale edges or tolerate spurious invalidations.  I think we could make invalidator users subscribe to a 'deleted task id bus' which would allow them to drop references, this could be useful and then the few cases where we _persist_ invalidators (by way of `State` objects) would need to  devise a new mechanism (or decide to tolerate the spurious invalidations)

prs.title: Remove the page/layout distinction from RouteTree
prs.author: acdlite
prs.body:
Part of a series of internal refactors to improve param tracking on the client.

A route tree node used to come in two variants, a layout and a page, distinguished by an isPage flag that every constructor had to keep consistent with the VaryPath it built. The variants only differed in whether the vary path carried a search params entry, and the code that needed to know either checked the flag or read the vary path's shape positionally.

Collapse them into one RouteTree type with one VaryPath type. The few places that still care whether a node is a page derive it from the segment. When something needs to read the search params, they can be accessed from the RouteTree or VaryPath like we do for other params.

This is a pure refactor of the existing code. It reads more naturally with a single tree type and a single vary path type, which the rest of this stack builds on.

prs.title: Turbopack: avoid project-wide traces from package directories
prs.author: sokra
prs.body:
### What?

Limit Turbopack's package-origin project-root tracing to statically named **files**, while resolving the complete original request relative to the package as before. This applies to filesystem, directory, child-process and Node worker references.

### Why?

Static does not necessarily mean narrow: `node-gyp-build`'s `path.resolve(dir || '.')` contains a static `'.'` branch. Tracing that from the application root as a directory recursively includes unrelated application assets. We still need packages to find explicitly named application config files.

### How?

Analysis records two candidate contexts without inspecting the filesystem: an optional app-root context for static file paths, and a package-local fallback for the original request. At reference resolution, the app-side lookup keeps only fully static file matches; directories and symlinked directories cannot recursively expand there. The package-side lookup independently traces the full pattern, including dynamic alternatives and directory contents. Both results are combined so even a mixed file/directory expression can retain its app config **and** package-local assets; the combination preserves distinct files sharing a request key and deduplicates identical modules. Protobuf `includeDirs` uses the same reference path.

Regression fixtures cover a `node-gyp-build`-style `'.'` fallback, mixed file/directory alternatives with same-named files in both contexts, symlinked directories and files, a missing optiona
…(truncated)

prs.author: unstubbable
prs.body:
Static root-param tracking for `'use cache'` needs to distinguish which getters a cached module imports. The existing generated module contains every getter, so module-level dependency collection includes unrelated root params.

`next/root-params` now re-exports each getter from a separate virtual module. The generated `next/root-params` module declares that it has no side effects, so Turbopack resolves named imports without including unrelated getter modules. Runtime root-param tracking remains unchanged.

The split also keeps code hashes stable when unrelated root params are added. The regression test checks this dependency isolation through the existing code-hash manifest.

prs.title: Avoid obsolete pnpm overrides in pack-next
prs.author: wbinnssmith
prs.body:
### What?

Make `pack-next` choose pnpm override locations from the destination workspace root's pinned `packageManager` version.

### Why?

pnpm 11+ warns about `pnpm.overrides` in `package.json` and ignores that setting. Conversely, rewriting `pnpm-workspace.yaml` for older pnpm versions creates unnecessary churn.

### How?

Use the repository's `semver` package to read the major from a pinned pnpm version. For a pnpm 11+ destination, merge overrides into the existing/detected pnpm workspace file without adding `pnpm.overrides` to `package.json`. For pnpm 10 and older, update only the package.json field. When the pin is missing or unusable, retain the previous dual-write behavior. Existing user overrides and npm/Yarn override behavior are preserved.

### Verification

- Passed eleven temporary destination scenarios covering pinned older/newer pnpm, existing overrides and workspace files, nested workspace roots, and unknown versions.
- Prettier check, Node syntax check, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Repo-wide lint/typecheck not run (root dependencies are not installed in this checkout).

prs.title: Fix Server Actions hanging after navigation to PPR pages
prs.author: unstubbable
prs.body:
Adopts #99229. Closes #99229.

A Server Action can hang on Vercel when the client navigates from `/a` to a PPR `/b` page and then calls an action owned by `/a`. The `/b` POST can carry postponed state. `app-page-runtime.ts` consumes the request stream to separate that state and saves the remaining action body as `actionBody`. The forwarding path reads `req.stream()` again, so its fetch waits on an exhausted stream until the function times out.

The forwarding path now sends `actionBody` when it is present. It removes the source route's resume headers because the forwarded body no longer contains that state; the platform can attach the target route's state on the new request. Requests without a saved action body still use the request stream.

The E2E test uses `connection()` to make `/b` PPR, warms its shell, navigates from `/a` to `/b`, and invokes an action imported only by `/a`. On a fresh Vercel deployment, it stays pending without this change and returns `pong` with it. The same test passes under `next start`, which does not receive the platform's prepended state.

Fixes #99153

prs.title: Hoist resolved pathname into app page route match
prs.author: gnoff
prs.body:
This PR was authored by codex but I'll share the motivation here in my own words. In an effort to improve the architectural underpinnings of Next.js we need to move away from a request/response dominated interface for rendering in Next.js. The legacy of this style is code that in some cases targets a fake Request or Response object even in cases where we are prerendering and no such objects actually exist. This PR adds a new concept of RouteMatch which seems overkill for only containing the resolvedPathname however we will be migrating more properties out of catchall context such as renderOpts and other request local context into more semantically meaningful packaging.

## Summary

Introduce a required `RouteMatch` containing the route-prepared `resolvedPathname` and pass it explicitly through the Node, Edge, direct server, and static export app-page render entrypoints.

The type is owned by the app-page route-module handler boundary rather than app-render. `resolvedPathname` is no longer written to or read from request metadata, preventing downstream code with request access from depending on that side channel while preserving the existing delimiter-safe pathname representation.
